skill.name: linkedin-voice
skill.description: Builds a LinkedIn voice card from three to five messages, improves drafts, and saves approved examples as a BeReach playbook.
skill.summary: Create an evidence-based writing profile for consistent LinkedIn outreach.
skill.author: bereach-ai

security_audit.summary: All 36 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting or ordinary prose. No evidence found of shell execution, weak cryptography, or system reconnaissance. A separate instruction suppresses user-requested cost information while requiring full briefing, creating a budget-control and transparency risk.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md lines 139-140 prohibit discussing credits or cost even when the user raises them.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the cost-suppression rule, answer budget questions directly, and obtain approval before any potentially chargeable briefing that exceeds the stated budget.

content.value_statement: Generic outreach drafts often lose the sender's writing style. This skill builds a voice card from real messages and checks new drafts against approved examples.
actual_capabilities: Extract greetings, sign-offs, punctuation, pronoun habits, sentence lengths, and signature phrases from three to five messages.
Record quoted evidence for voice-card fields and keep unsupported fields empty.
Separate consistent writing habits from tone differences across invitations, first messages, follow-ups, and replies.
Apply companion message frameworks to revise examples while retaining the sender's identity and stated writing restrictions.
Save approved examples and writing guidelines as a language-specific BeReach playbook when the required tools are available.
Check drafts for voice consistency, forbidden phrases, address form, and invented facts or offers.
limitations: Full operation depends on BeReach tools and companion skills that are not included in these four files.
A small sample supports style guidance, not reliable authorship identification or guaranteed outreach results.
The files define drafting and review guidance, not a standalone application or message-sending integration.
The current instructions suppress cost discussion; resolve this audit concern before relying on potentially chargeable briefings.

use_cases.title: Keep founder outreach personal
use_cases.description: Turn a founder's own successful conversations into a reusable writing profile for new prospect drafts.
use_cases.target_user: Founders handling their own LinkedIn outreach

use_cases.title: Standardize individual seller profiles
use_cases.description: Create separate evidence-based voice cards so representatives retain their own greetings, vocabulary, and message tone.

use_cases.title: Maintain language-specific client voices
use_cases.description: Build approved cards for each client's language and review drafts against their address forms and forbidden wording.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze my writing samples
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a draft voice card from these three messages I wrote: [paste messages]. Quote evidence for each field and leave unsupported fields empty.

prompt_templates.title: Check a draft against my voice
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this draft with my approved voice card: [paste both]. Fix mismatches in greeting, address form, punctuation, and forbidden wording.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review an existing outreach draft.

prompt_templates.title: Create a reference and test message
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my samples, a real recipient, and verified facts: [paste inputs]. Apply the available companion frameworks and explain revisions. Draft only; do not send.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: validate style on a new recipient.

prompt_templates.title: Update an approved saved playbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my saved playbook and these repeated corrections: [paste corrections]. Propose scoped changes and request approval before saving. Ask before any chargeable tool use.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: maintain persistent writing guidance with explicit approval.

best_practices: Provide varied messages you wrote and identify which received substantive replies.
Review quoted evidence and approve revised samples before saving a playbook containing conversation text.
Confirm tool costs, data access, and save scope before approving BeReach operations.
anti_patterns: Using unedited generated messages as proof of your personal writing style.
Treating a few positive replies as proof that a message framework improves response rates.
Approving tool usage without understanding costs or which conversation excerpts will be stored.

faq.question: How many writing samples are needed?
faq.answer: The workflow asks for three to five varied messages you wrote, preferably messages that received substantive replies.

faq.question: Can I start without answered messages?
faq.answer: Yes. Unanswered messages support form observations only. A corrected test message becomes the first sample, and the card remains provisional.

faq.question: What does the voice card record?
faq.answer: It records greetings, sign-offs, address form, punctuation, pronouns, signature phrases, forbidden wording, and tone by message type.

faq.question: Does the skill send LinkedIn messages?
faq.answer: These files describe analysis, drafting, checking, and playbook storage. They do not define a message-sending step.

faq.question: Where are approved writing examples saved?
faq.answer: With BeReach tool access and user approval, revised examples and guidelines are saved as a language-specific playbook.

faq.question: Are BeReach tool costs addressed safely?
faq.answer: The audit identified an instruction suppressing cost discussion. Resolve that instruction and confirm applicable charges before using full briefings.
